_comment: Golden set for the ustudent-handbook RAG system. Used informally in lesson 7 for workshop acceptance, formally in lesson 10 for evaluation. Each item has a question, a reference answer, and a flag for whether the handbook actually contains the answer (used to test the 'I don't know' fallback).

items.q: How many credits do I need to graduate?
items.ref: 120 credits, with a cumulative GPA of at least 2.0.

items.q: What is the maximum credits I can take in one semester?
items.ref: 18 credits. To exceed 18 you need a GPA of 3.5 or higher and written approval from Academic Advising.
Usually not. CS201 requires sophomore standing or higher and at least 30 completed credit hours, plus CS101 as a prerequisite.

GPA is the credit-weighted average of grade points across graded courses. Multiply each course's grade points by its credits, sum, then divide by total credits. Withdrawn (W) and incomplete (I) courses are excluded.

items.q: What is the difference between dropping and withdrawing?
items.ref: Dropping happens in Weeks 1-4 and removes the course from your transcript entirely (full or partial refund depending on week). Withdrawing happens in Weeks 5-8, leaves a W on the transcript, does not affect GPA, and carries no refund.
